provenance.instrument: 2011 Zoning Ordinance of the Borough of Wilson (Chapter 170 Zoning, Ord. No. 760 of 12-27-2012, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 WI0763, Borough of Wilson, Northampton County (170-23 'Borough': 'The Borough of Wilson, located in Northampton County'). Each district article lists its by-right, special exception and conditional uses and its lot and yard figures as text. The Table of Use Regulations (170-82) and Table 2 of parking spaces (170-95A) are PDF attachments and were not opened. Floodplain rules are in 170-86A and Chapter 110. New Laws: none
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 02-09-2026.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.' 170-22 carries Ord. No. 820 of 2-9-2026
checks: In-law suite: a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board in R-1, R-2 and TC (170-30H, 170-35J, 170-45O). 'One in-law suite to a residential dwelling shall be permitted, provided that the conditions set forth in this subsection are met' (170-83H(9)). A special exception needs a site plan certified by an engineer, surveyor, architect or landscape architect and Planning Commission review (170-11, 170-15)

The suite 'shall occupy no more than 25% of the total usable floor area of the principal residence, not including any garage', may have its own cooking, sleeping, living and bathroom facilities, and is limited to one per dwelling (170-83H(9)(a), (b), (e))

'In-law suites shall be part of the principal residence or may be contained in the existing accessory structure such as a garage. No new separate structures on the same lot with the principal residence shall be permitted to be constructed for this use' (170-83H(9)(c))

'The intent of these provisions is to allow for related family members to reside on the premises' (170-83H(9)). The section sets no family test of its own. Ask the zoning officer whether the Board will require relatives

The code's definition of an accessory dwelling unit, 'A separate second dwelling unit which may be located within a structure in which the principal use is for a single-family dwelling', allows it only if it has at most three rooms or 800 sq ft of livable area or 40% of the residential floor area (not counting basement and attic), whichever is less, is not meant for more than two people, stays in the same ownership as the house, and the owner lives in the principal unit (170-23 'Dwelling' H). A single-family detached dwelling is for one family 'except for an accessory dwelling unit' (170-23 'Dwelling' C). Whether these conditions bind an in-law suite is read as yes, since the suite is a second dwelling unit

Each in-law suite must be registered with the Borough Code Enforcement Officer, and the Northampton County Department of Human Services or another agency must certify that the wastewater facilities can serve the house and the suite (170-83H(9)(f), (g))

Parking: the house's required spaces 'plus one additional off-street parking space for the in-law suite' (170-83H(9)(d)). The house's own count is in Table 2, a PDF attachment that was not opened (170-95A)

R-1 and R-2 list 'Average lot area per dwelling unit' of 6,000 and 5,000 sq ft for a single-family detached lot (170-32B, 170-37A(2)). Whether the in-law suite counts as a dwelling unit for this figure is not settled

R-2 permits a two-family dwelling by right: two units 'entirely separated by vertical walls or horizontal floors', on 5,000 sq ft with 2,500 sq ft per unit (170-34C, 170-37C, 170-83B(2)). Multifamily dwellings of three or more units are a special exception in R-2 and TC on 20,000 sq ft (170-35A, 170-45A, 170-83B(3))

TC lists no single-family or two-family dwelling, only an in-law suite and multifamily dwellings by special exception (170-44, 170-45). A house there is read as a nonconforming use, which may be enlarged by no more than 40% (170-92A)

Floodplain: 'All structures, with the exception of those specifically allowed in § 170-86A(4)' are prohibited in the floodplain, and new construction in the floodway is prohibited (170-86A(1)(i), (5)(b), (c)). 'Within any identified floodplain area, unless a variance is requested and obtained, any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited' (110-22). An accessory structure in the floodplain 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may have at most 200 sq ft (110-22E). Improving an existing structure in the FF or FA area by 10% or more of its market value needs full floodproofing (170-86A(6)(d)[1]). The Zoning Hearing Board may grant floodplain variances, but none that raise the base flood elevation (170-86A(8))

Riparian buffer: 75 ft from the top of the streambank of a watercourse or the edge of a wetland, where all structures are prohibited, and principal structures stay 25 ft beyond the buffer (170-86C(1)(b), (c), (3)(a)). Development within 100 ft of a stream or of a pond over 1/4 acre needs special exception review (170-86E(4))

Steep slopes: where more than 5,000 sq ft is disturbed, structures on slopes of 15% to 25% are a conditional use and on slopes of 25% or more are prohibited (170-86F(3)(a), (6), (8)). Wetlands: no building may be built or enlarged in a wetland, and a lot needs 75% of its minimum area outside wetlands (170-86B(4), (5))

Nonconforming lot in R-1 or R-2 held alone: a single-family dwelling with any attached permitted accessory use may be built on 3,500 sq ft, 35 ft wide, front 25 ft, rear 15 ft, sides 3 ft and 11 ft together, coverage 50% (170-88F(1)(a))

Accessory buildings: sheds and similar buildings at most 15 ft tall. Detached garages at least 4 ft from the side and rear lines, behind the house's front building line and at most 15 ft tall (170-83H(3)(c), (d)). Two principal buildings on one lot must each meet the rules as if on its own lot (170-89A)

The conditional use G-16 'Lawful use not otherwise permitted' reaches only a use 'that is required to be permitted by the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code' (170-83G(16)). Variances: 170-17, with no bar on a use variance
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Borough of Wilson Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-17. Read: Article II, Article III (170-23), Articles V, VI and VIII, Article XIII from 170-79 to 170-83F(4) and 170-83G(16), H(3), H(9), 170-86, Article XV, Article XVI, Chapter 110 from 110-1 to 110-27C and code searches. Not read: Article I beyond 170-6, Article IV, Articles VII (H-1), IX (C-1), X (C-2), XI (I-1), XII (PRD overlay), XVII, XVIII (Redevelopment Overlay), 170-83 G except G-16 and H except H-3 and H-9, 170-84, 170-85, 170-87, the PDF attachments (Table of Use Regulations, Table 2 parking) and Chapter 110 after 110-27C (variances, definitions). A code search finds 'H-9 In-law suite' only in R-1, R-2 and TC. Open points: whether the accessory dwelling unit definition (800 sq ft, two people, owner occupancy) binds an in-law suite, whether the Board will require relatives, and whether the suite counts toward the average lot area per dwelling unit.

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-2)
value.conditions: A detached or semidetached building with not more than two dwelling units, entirely separated by vertical walls or horizontal floors, unpierced except for access to the outside or a common cellar. Lot 5,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide and 100 ft deep, with 2,500 sq ft per unit. Front and rear 25 ft, side 8 ft and 16 ft for both. Building coverage at most 45%. No family or owner rule

requires.condition: A lot at least 50 ft wide

value.note: A two-unit building, not an in-law suite. The code does not say how an existing house becomes one, so ask the zoning officer

historic_bypass.note: No historic path was found in the parts read

value.condition: The stated intent of the in-law suite rules is 'to allow for related family members to reside on the premises'. The section sets no family test, but the Board may ask for one.

Under the code's accessory dwelling unit definition the unit may have at most three rooms, is not meant for more than two people, stays in the same ownership as the house, and the owner must live in the principal unit.

The suite must be registered with the Borough Code Enforcement Officer, and the Northampton County Department of Human Services or another agency must certify that the wastewater facilities can serve the house and the suite.
TC lists no single-family or two-family dwelling. A house there is a nonconforming use, which may be enlarged by no more than 40% of its floor or ground area.

In the floodplain 'All structures, with the exception of those specifically allowed in § 170-86A(4)' are prohibited, and none of those is a dwelling or an addition to one. New construction in the floodway is prohibited.
An accessory structure in the identified floodplain area 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation', may have at most 200 sq ft and may have no sanitary facilities.

In the floodplain, new construction and substantial improvements are prohibited unless a variance is obtained, and then the lowest floor must be at or above the regulatory flood elevation. Improving an existing structure by 10% or more of its market value needs full floodproofing.
The riparian buffer is 75 ft from the top of the streambank of a watercourse, and principal structures stay at least 25 ft beyond the buffer. All structures are prohibited in the buffer.

Development within 100 ft of the normal streambank of a river or stream, or of a pond over 1/4 acre, needs special exception review. Within 75 ft of a wetland's edge all structures are prohibited, and no building may be built or enlarged in a wetland.
Where more than 5,000 sq ft of land is disturbed, a structure on a slope of 15% to 25% is a conditional use and on a slope of 25% or more is prohibited.

types_allowed.note: 'In-law suites shall be part of the principal residence or may be contained in the existing accessory structure such as a garage.' An addition is read as part of the residence

types_not_addressed.note: A suite in an existing garage is allowed. Adding a story to a garage is not named, and garages may be at most 15 ft tall

max_share_of_house.note: 'no more than 25% of the total usable floor area of the principal residence, not including any garage'

max_sqft.note: From the accessory dwelling unit definition: three rooms or 800 sq ft of livable area or 40% of the residential floor area, whichever is less. Read as binding the in-law suite

family_only.note: Only an intent statement: 'to allow for related family members to reside on the premises'

occupancy.value: Not meant for more than two people. The stated intent is for related family members.

owner_occupancy.note: 'the principal unit shall be occupied by the owner of the structure at all times'. From the accessory dwelling unit definition

max_adus.note: 'No more than one in-law suite shall be permitted per residential dwelling.'

sale_apart_allowed.note: 'The entire dwelling structure, including both the principal and the accessory dwelling unit, shall remain in the same ownership at all times'

setback_side_ft.note: A detached garage may be 4 ft from the side and rear lines. The suite may use only an existing garage

max_height_ft.note: 'Garages shall not exceed 15 feet in height.'

spaces_required.note: 'The required off-street parking for the principal dwelling plus one additional off-street parking space for the in-law suite'

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: 'Average lot area per dwelling unit (square feet): 6,000.' Whether the suite counts is not settled

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached: 5,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide. Semidetached 3,000 sq ft, 30 ft wide

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: 'Average lot area per dwelling unit (square feet): 5,000' for a single-family detached lot, 3,000 for a semidetached one. Whether the suite counts is not settled

setback_sides_total_ft.note: Semidetached: one side yard of 8 ft

max_building_coverage.note: 45% for a semidetached or two-family dwelling

min_lot_sqft.note: 5,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide, 100 ft deep. The average lot area per dwelling unit is left blank
